transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 min
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood CSM), Jared (CTO - MagnetWell), Mina (Lead ML Eng), Samir (SRE), Lena (PM)

Summary:
MagnetWell is evaluating hosting modes (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) with an emphasis on p95 latency targets for low-latency interactive features and high-throughput token/sec batch scoring. Primary constraints: sub-300ms p95 for 512-token streaming responses, peak concurrency ~1.2k concurrent open streams, periodic token storms of 150k tokens/sec for 3-5 minutes in burst scenarios. Discussed tradeoffs, KV cache strategies, quantization and routing/fallbacks. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run a short token/sec benchmark plan on Dedicated, share security docs and pricing.

Topics (auto): Hosting modes; p95 targets; Streaming vs non-streaming; Concurrency modeling; Token/sec benchmarking; Security and compliance

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, quick round of intros?
00:05 Jared: Jared Cole, CTO, MagnetWell. We're trying to understand whether to go hosted, reserved/dedicated, or private e.g. VPC-hosted behind our network.
00:10 Mina: Mina, ML lead. I'm mostly worried about the p95 when we do streaming multi-turn assistant stuff.
00:15 Samir: Samir, SRE, I'll own the oper side and hard SLOs.
00:18 Alex: Great. Priya, do you want to run the agenda?
00:20 Priya: Sure. We'll cover current workload profile, p95 targets, concurrency and streaming profile, then tradeoffs and suggested benchmark plan. We'll also cover security asks.
00:28 Lena: Quick note — we have a product launch in mid-September and need a decision by Aug 15 if possible. Tight timeline.
00:34 Priya: Got it, that helps. Can you share current numbers — qps, tokens per request, and what p95 you target today?
00:40 Mina: Right now in-house we see average request size 220 tokens, but longer flows hit 500-600 tokens. For the assistant use-case we need p95 under 300 milliseconds for streaming-first experience for approx 512 token responses. Today we get like 800–1,200ms p95 which is too slow.
00:58 Alex: Ok that's useful. And concurrency?
01:02 Mina: At steady-state we expect 250 concurrent conversations, but peak spikes up to 1,200 concurrent open streaming sessions during promos. Also occasionally the scoring pipeline will flood with token bursts, say 100–150k tokens/sec for short 3–5min bursts during events.
01:20 Priya: Nice detail. So two distinct workloads: low-latency streaming with many concurrent connections, and short high-throughput token storms. Both are solvable but we pick different levers — dedicated pools for predictable tail latency, plus KV prefix caching and transient autoscaling for bursts.
01:38 Samir: Two immediate asks: 1) we need predictable p95 to keep frontend SLAs; 2) we need audit logs and KMS integration for keying.
01:47 Alex: On the KMS side we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via KMS integration — real note: we'll share the KMS doc. For hosted there's envelope encryption and SOC2 but not CMK.
01:58 Mina: That's important. Also what's the realistic p95 we can expect with Hosted? We have a concern that hosted might have variable tails because of multi-tenant cold starts.
02:10 Priya: For streaming short responses on our hosted tier we've seen p95 in the 180–320ms range for 256–512 token responses depending on model and region; dedicated pools consistently hit lower tails — think 120–220ms p95 — because you control the GPU pool and we can pin model variants/quantization. But hosted gives the fastest time to value.
02:33 Jared: So dedicated seems attractive. What about cost delta roughly? We want to know opex delta vs hosted.
02:41 Alex: We'll send a detailed pricing sheet but rough rule — dedicated moves you from pure usage to a committed pool model. Per-token cost can drop significantly especially with batching and cache. But you pay baseline reserved capacity. For token storms, dedicated + autoscale/burst works well.
02:58 Mina: Can you explain how KV cache prefixing would help streaming p95? I know the theory but not the operational details.
03:06 Priya: Sure. If many requests share initial prefixes or system prompts we can cache KV states so future requests avoid recomputing earlier layers. That reduces per-token compute. In streaming cases it cuts steady-state token generation work. Also continuous batching for non-streaming scoring requests increases throughput without hurting tails much.
03:28 Samir: Any caveats re: state eviction or memory pressure on KV caches in multi-tenant hosted?
03:32 Priya: In hosted we limit per-tenant KV retention and use weighted eviction; in dedicated private you control retention policy and memory sizes. For MagnetWell's burst profile, dedicated gives much more flexibility.
03:44 Lena: On Private / VPC option — we'd need on-prem or VPC peering because of HIPAA concerns for some workflows. Does Redwood Private support HSM/KMS?
03:53 Alex: Yes, Private can integrate with your KMS/HSM and on-prem package is available for air-gapped needs. We'll attach the compliance matrix.
04:03 Mina: Ok good. Let's pivot to benchmarking — can Redwood run a small benchmark to validate p95 and token/sec for us?
04:12 Priya: Yes. Our usual plan: we run a 48-hour token/sec run on a dedicated pool with your representative prompts and one hosted quick run for baseline. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99, end-to-end streaming latency including first-byte, and tokens/sec sustained for 5-minute windows and 1-minute windows. We'll also test fallback behavior and cold start degradation.
04:35 Jared: What inputs do you need from us?
04:37 Priya: Samples of prompts, typical payload sizes, expected concurrency curve (minute-by-minute or hour-by-hour), and target SLOs. We'll want a small test harness or can run our generator if you share templates.
04:47 Mina: I'll put together 10 prompt templates and token distribution.
04:50 Samir: How do you simulate network jitter? Our users are global and we see variable region latency.
04:56 Priya: We can run regionally in us-west, eu-west and apply synthetic network latencies. Also we test with different model variants and quantization paths — quantized 4-bit vs fp16 — to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
05:12 Alex: Quick question from Jared earlier — are there any auto-fallbacks if dedicated pool saturates?
05:18 Priya: Yes, policy-based routing can fallback to compatible variants or hosted instances. You can configure hard fail vs degrade modes. We'll show a canary and fallback config in the benchmark.
05:28 Jared: Ok I want to dig into numbers — what's a good baseline for 512 token streaming p95 on A100 class hardware vs H100, and how does batching affect that?
05:39 Priya: Ballpark: on H100 with optimized kernels and fq4 quant we often see ~100–160ms p95 for 512 tokens in dedicated streaming optimized runtime; on A100 it's typically +20–40% tail depending on kernel support. Continuous batching helps non-streaming. For streaming, batching only applies to initial prefix or mixed-request scenarios; too much batching can hurt streaming first-byte.
06:05 Mina: And tokens/sec? If we need to sustain 150k tokens/sec for bursts, what pool size would you recommend?
06:12 Priya: It depends on model size and quant. For a 7B-class model quantized 4-bit, you'd likely need 6–8 H100-equivalent GPUs to sustain 150k tokens/sec with margin. For 13B-class it could be double. We'll propose a specific config in the benchmark plan.
06:28 Samir: That helps. Another SRE question: do you support per-route rate limits and graceful throttling with headers so our frontend can degrade gracefully?
06:36 Alex: Yes, per-route quotas, token-level cost headers, and explicit retry-after semantics. We'll send the docs.
06:42 Lena: On security, we need SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit trails — are these in the enterprise bundle?
06:50 Alex: Yes, SOC2/ISO are standard for enterprise; SAML SSO and RBAC and retention controls are in enterprise. We'll attach the security pack. For Private we can map to your internal audit stack.
06:59 Mina: There's often a gap between theoretical p95 numbers and real app -- e.g., frontend assembling tokens and network overhead. Can we run an E2E synthetic from our staging with your dedicated pool?
07:09 Priya: Absolutely — we can set up a VPC peered dedicated test and run an E2E harness from your staging infra. That will capture network and client-side assembly overheads.
07:19 Jared: Good. One concern: if we use hosted initially and later migrate to dedicated/private, how disruptive is that?
07:25 Alex: We built the API to be consistent — same client calls, model naming. Migration is mostly config-level: pin model versions, update routing to the dedicated endpoint, and a short validation. We can help with a migration runbook.
07:36 Mina: Ok, let's talk about metrics we'll want from the benchmark report — p50/p95/p99 per region, tokens/sec sustained and burst, cost per 1k tokens for each mode, and KV cache hit rates.
07:47 Priya: We'll include all that, plus the per-route latency breakdown and token-level cost header samples. We'll also include whether quantization caused any measurable regen quality regressions for your prompts.
07:58 Samir: On the quality front: we need to be careful with aggressive quantization if it changes hallucination or answer fidelity. Do you run evals tied to prompt sets?
08:06 Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will run evals and quality regressions on prompt sets — we can run your ground-truth checks as part of the plan.
08:13 Lena: Timeline recap — we're aiming for decision by Aug 15. Can Redwood commit to pushing benchmark results by Aug 6 so we can review?
08:20 Alex: Yes, if we get assets by July 31 we can run the 48-hour benchmark and aim to deliver results by Aug 6.
08:27 Jared: Great. Minor nit — do you log prompt content in hosted? We have sensitive PII in some prompts.
08:34 Alex: Hosted by default redacts PII in storage and has configurable retention; for full control you want Private or Dedicated with customer-managed retention. We'll put that in the security doc.
08:42 Mina: For test harness we have some long context + tool calls, so we also want to simulate function/tool calling overheads.
08:49 Priya: We'll include function-call payloads and multi-turn flows. We'll simulate tool latencies and measure end-to-end.
08:55 Jared: Any other gotchas we should be aware of?
09:00 Priya: Cold-starts and model variant compatibility are typical; we'll show warmup policies, checkpoint preloads, and hot cache strategies. Also routing for multi-region failover if a region gets saturated.
09:12 Samir: For autoscale during bursts, how fast can you spin up extra nodes?
09:16 Priya: With pre-warmed images and burst pools we can scale in 30–90 seconds depending on the backend. For strict SLOs we recommend a small reserved buffer plus a burst pool to avoid hitting cold-start tails.
09:29 Mina: That probably fits. Anything else on pricing?
09:32 Alex: Pricing note: we'll show committed pool examples and a hybrid — keep base steady on dedicated and route overflow to hosted for cost efficiency.
09:41 Daniel (CSM): From a customer success angle we'll schedule a check-in after the benchmark to walk the report.
09:46 Alex: Great. Quick recap and ownerships: Priya -> benchmark plan and run; Alex -> security docs + pricing; Mina -> prompt templates + token projections; Samir -> network constraints and SLOs; Daniel -> schedule follow-up. Everyone ok?
09:59 Jared: Yep.
10:00 Lena: Yes.
10:02 Alex: We'll target the Aug 6 delivery. Thanks all.
10:06 (meeting ends)
